results.content: # Design and implement a retention strategy for pipeline artifacts and dependencies. In this guide, you’ll learn how to set up and manage retention policies in Azure Pipelines. Retention policies in Azure DevOps automatically purge old runs, artifacts, and attachments based on configurable rules. You can scope retention settings to specific branches, tags, or pipeline triggers. ## Configure Retention in the Azure DevOps UI. ## Define Retention in Your Pipeline YAML. trigger: branches: [ main ] pool: vmImage: ubuntu-latest variables: retentionDays: 30 jobs: - job: Build displayName: Build and Publish Artifact steps: - script: echo "Compiling source code..." displayName: Compile Code - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1 inputs: pathToPublish: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)' artifactName: 'drop' - job: Cleanup displayName: Clean Up and Create Retention Lease dependsOn: Build pool: server steps: - task: DeleteFiles@1 inputs: SourceFolder: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)' Contents: '**/*.tmp' displayName: Remove Temporary Files - task: PowerShell@2 inputs: targetType: 'inline' script: | $uri = "$(System.CollectionUri)$(System.TeamProject)/_apis/build/retention/leases? | Azure DevOps UI | Centralized retention settings in Project Settings | N/A |. Centralize retention variables in a template to keep your pipelines DRY and maintainable.
